day.unavailable: The day horizon needs daily bars; the upstream feed commits Friday closes only.

why: XLB +1.17 pct to $49.43 matched SPY (+0.01 pts) but did not close above a level that matters: rejected three times at $49.64-49.73 (20D), a fourth straight weekly close under the 200D ($50.36), $47.81 untested -- 'a hold of the low, not a reversal' (wiki/materials.md; macro/facts.json).

The restriction on new commodity longs (#115) stays ON: DXY 102.21, a third weekly close above 101, a fourth straight weekly gain, 0.03 under the 52-week closing high, and this leg rose with December hike odds -- the orthodox direction (wiki/materials.md; wiki/canary-watch.md CROSS-ASSET SIGNALS).

Construction materials made new lows under a 5.60 pct 30Y and a 7.40 pct mortgage: MLM at a one-year closing low, CRH 8 cents above its low, VMC $3.75 above; the row stays untouchable while the 30-year makes highs (wiki/materials.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 4 item 5).

Week RF raised 30 -> 32 and MC held at 40: the only Monday input is copper's settlement against $6.60 (Friday-evening last trade $6.64, December $6.69 -- provisional); CPI Wed is the dollar's gate; AA and CMC Thu are the week's only prints (wiki/materials.md EARNINGS CALENDAR).
risks: Bullish falsifier: copper holds $6.60 at Monday's settlement with DXY at 102 -- 'the rule is being tested by the tape, not by me'; steel's rally (CLF +14.7, NUE +4.1, STLD +2.8 pct) converts ISM prices paid 77.9 into earnings Oct 19-26; a close over $50.36 with the 20D reclaimed ends the sub-200D streak (wiki/materials.md Ophelia and Marky).
Falsifier: DXY makes a new 52-week high and every commodity long pays again; a close under $47.81 completes the move to $47.00 (wiki/materials.md).
CLF closed above its $12.60 mean target into an Oct 19 print with an ~11 pct implied move -- 'a risk, not a signal' (wiki/materials.md; wiki/synthesis.md Section 1).

Data under the page moves: last week's gold -3.7 / silver -6.6 pct were continuous-contract artifacts (settled gold +1.4 pct to $4,191 GCV26); CTVA/VYLR history is unadjusted post-spin (wiki/materials.md WILD CARD; wiki/synthesis.md Section 7.A).

why: Month arithmetic is weak (breadth 30, relative momentum 30, -5.10 pts vs SPY) and the regime is the dollar: the restriction re-opens only below 99.00 and the dollar is 102.21 (wiki/materials.md; macro/facts.json).

The commodity complex 'did not behave this week the way a restriction-justifying dollar should make it behave': gold settled +1.4 pct with the 10Y real yield flat (~2.91 pct), copper +2.3 pct, steel 3-15 pct -- the evidence against the rule is on the page and the rule survives (wiki/materials.md Ophelia Verdict; wiki/canary-watch.md CROSS-ASSET SIGNALS).

Month RF held at 33 and MC held at 45: CLF/STLD Oct 19, KALU Oct 21, NEM/DOW Oct 22, NUE Oct 26, FCX/SHW/ECL/PPG Oct 27, LIN/VMC/CRH Oct 29, MLM Nov 3, ALB Nov 4; CTVA/VYLR's first standalone prints moved to Nov 11, outside the window (wiki/materials.md EARNINGS CALENDAR).
risks: The 30Y keeps rising (mortgages 7.40 pct) -> MLM, CRH, VMC extend lows and FY guides are cut in late October (wiki/materials.md RISK SCENARIOS).
Mercer is not alone: a second SMID materials issuer misses a payment (#99); Mercer's noteholder talks have no signed support agreement found (wiki/materials.md SMALL/MID-CAP WATCH).

Bullish falsifier: China stimulus after Golden Week (Shanghai reopened Oct 8, no dated read found) or DXY back under 101 softens the restriction; MLM at a one-year closing low with a 33 pct gap to target is 'the first name I study when the 30-year stops rising' (wiki/materials.md).

extracts.lead_summary: The dollar did not give an inch and the sector bounced anyway. DXY closed 102.21 — a third weekly close above 101 and within three hundredths of the year's closing high — so the restriction on new commodity longs stays ON. XLB rose 1.2% to $49.43, a rebound from last week's low, on steel (CLF +14.7%, NUE +4.1%), a Corteva that is up 9% as two companies, and a gold price that settled higher, not lower. I have to correct my own page: the -3.7% gold I printed last week was a continuous-contract artifact; the October contract settled $4,133.70, and this week's $4,191 is +1.4%. The $6.60 copper rail I called broken is back — provisionally, on Friday-evening prints. Ophelia stays restricted; the tape is not asking her permission.
